predecessors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
predecessors.text: 'Pagus of Blois', the county's predecessor in the infobox: 'the title was formally created in 832, when King Louis the Pious made Adrian's second son count'

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: the county's cells: Cliopatria's Kingdom of France shape of 1402 holds 14 of the 15 cells of the 1401 Blois shape

successors.name: Duchy of Orléans
successors.text: Blois held by Louis I, Duke of Orleans: 'Count of Blois from 1397 to 1407'

ledger.x: 832: Louis the Pious creates the county of Blois.

c. 940: Theobald I holds Tours, Chartres and Châteaudun with Blois. The page says Blois passed to him 'around 940' and that 'he was also count of Tours, Chartres and Châteaudun'; it does not date the three counties, so the year bridges a silence.
1037: Odo II dies and Stephen II takes Troyes, Meaux and Vitry.
1044: Geoffrey Martel takes Touraine at Nouy.
1063: Theobald III reunites Blois and Champagne.
1125: Theobald IV of Blois becomes Count of Champagne.
1142: Louis VII's war on Theobald II of Champagne begins.
1144: the war with Louis VII ends.
1152: Theobald IV dies and his lands divide.
1230: the Avesnes branch takes the county.
1241: Blois-Châtillon takes the county and holds it 'until 1397'; the page gives no year for the start of the Châtillon counts, 1241 follows the end of the Avesnes years.
1286: Joan, Countess of Blois, sells Chartres.

ledger.cp: Châteaudun (holder not named by the pages opened)

ledger.x: 1397: Blois passes from the Châtillon counts to the Duke of Orleans.

wars.name: Battle of Pontlevoy
wars.outcome: Odo II 'Defeated by Fulk III of Anjou and Herbert I of Maine at the Battle of Pontlevoy in July 1016'.

wars.name: Odo II's invasion of the Kingdom of Burgundy
wars.outcome: 'In 1032, he invaded the Kingdom of Burgundy on the death of Rudolph III'; he retreated against a coalition of Conrad II and Henry I.

wars.name: Odo II's invasion of Lorraine
wars.outcome: Odo invaded Lorraine in 1037 and died in the rout at Bar-le-Duc, defeated by Gothelo I, on 15 November 1037; his domains were divided between Theobald III and Stephen II.

wars.name: Geoffrey Martel's conquest of Touraine
wars.outcome: Geoffrey Martel besieged Tours; at Nouy Theobald III was captured and gave up Touraine to regain his freedom.

wars.name: Louis VII's war against Theobald II of Champagne
wars.outcome: The conflict 'lasted two years (1142-1144)'; Champagne was occupied by the royal army and Vitry-le-François captured.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines in the pages opened; the Loire counties are fief boundaries.
